name: Mehrabian-Russell PAD Model
citation: Mehrabian, A. & Russell, J.A. (1974). An approach to environmental psychology. MIT Press.
rejection_rationale: Fully reduces to IC + NM + DP without residual. Pleasure maps to IC valence (interoceptive prediction error direction), Arousal maps to NM sympathetic activation, Dominance maps to DP perceived control. No organizing principle unique to PAD remains after this decomposition — it is a dimensionality claim, not a domain theory.
key_references: Mehrabian, A. & Russell, J.A. (1974). An approach to environmental psychology. MIT Press.

function_form.function_form: E(s) = [P(s), A(s), D(s)]ᵀ; P = pleasure, A = arousal, D = dominance

variables.E(s): Emotional state in response to stimulus s (3D vector)

predictions: Environmental pleasure accounts for ~50% of emotional variance
Arousal × dominance interaction predicts approach-avoidance behavior

provenance.seminal_paper: Mehrabian, A. & Russell, J.A. (1974). An approach to environmental psychology. Cambridge: MIT Press.
provenance.validation_paper: Russell, J.A. & Mehrabian, A. (1977). Evidence for a three-factor theory of emotions. Journal of Research in Personality, 11(3), 273-294.
provenance.predecessor: Dimensional approaches to emotion (Schlosberg's two-dimensional theory of emotion); arousal theory; ecological perception
provenance.historical_context: Mehrabian and Russell developed the PAD (Pleasure-Arousal-Dominance) model to explain how physical environments influence human emotional states and behavior. Original purpose was environmental psychology theory — proposing that physical environments primarily affect people through their emotional/affective impact via three independent dimensions. Pleasure-Displeasure reflects positive vs. negative emotional valence; Arousal-Nonarousal reflects stimulation and activation level; Dominance-Submissiveness reflects sense of control and influence within the environment.
key_milestones: 1974: Mehrabian & Russell foundational work establishing PAD framework
1977: Russell & Mehrabian validation paper confirming three-factor structure
1980s-1990s: Development of semantic differential scales for measurement
1980s-Present: Extensive application to consumer psychology, HCI, environmental design, emotion research
influenced_by: James A. Russell (emotion theory, dimensional approaches)
James J. Gibson (ecological perception, environmental affordances)
provenance.current_status: foundational framework widely applied across psychology, marketing, design, and human-computer interaction
provenance.verification_notes: Seminal paper (1974) verified via MIT Press publications. Russell & Mehrabian (1977) validation paper verified via Journal of Research in Personality. Original application to environmental psychology (not just emotion generally) confirmed via multiple design and environmental psychology sources. Google Scholar citation count confirmed at 6,000+. Three-dimension structure (Pleasure, Arousal, Dominance) verified across semantic differential measurement literature.
